A B S T R A C T
A defect free copper interconnect is crucial for ensuring the electrical connection and transmission of high
density interconnect printed circuit boards. Leveling agent is a key regulatory factor for achieving dense cop
per super filling from bottom to top in blind holes during the electroplating process of high-density interconnect
boards. Here, two small molecule five-membered heterocyclic compounds with different side chains, namely 3-
amino-5-mercapto-1,2,4-triazole (AMT) and 2–5-methyl-1,3,4-thiadiazole (MMT), were selected to be as level-
ling agents to study their effect on the copper filling behavior on blind holes. Electrochemical tests including
cyclic voltammetry solvation (CV) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) were firstly used to analyze the inhib-
itory effect of two leveling agents on copper deposition and it was indicated that the MMT has a more significant
inhibitory effect on the copper deposition than the AMT. Subsequently, the influence of different concentrations
of MMT on the inhibition of copper deposition and the blind hole filling performance were also further analyzed
by LSV, CV, and constant current measurement (GM), where an optimal concentration of 7 ppm was obtained for
the maximum inhibitory ability on the copper deposition accompanied by the best blind hole filling ability. The
characterization analysis from the field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), atomic force micro-
scopy (AFM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) also illuminates that the MMT leveling agent can effectively reduce the
surface roughness of copper filled with micropores and promote the selective growth of copper coatings along the
(11 1) crystallographic plane. The adsorption behavior of the levelling agent on the cathode surface during
electrodeposition was further also studied by the quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics sim
ulations combined with the in situ electrochemical surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy (EC-SERS) experi-
ments. It has been suggested that the thiol, sulfur, and alkyl groups in the leveling agent MMT molecule are
nucleophilic groups, providing preferred active sites for adsorption reactions and thus generating effective in-
hibition ability on copper deposition formation. Thermal shock experiments based on tin immersion showed the
copper layer obtained under the addition of the levelling agent MMT has excellent reliability. The comprehensive
results indicated that 2-mercapto-5-methyl-1,3,4-thiadiazole (MMT) was an effective levelling agent for the blind
hole supperfilling.

depth-to-diameter ratios [4]. In the process of copper plating on such

significant difference between a current’s density distribution inside and
on the surface of the micro vias. In such an environment, the copper

3. Results and discussion
3.1. Electrochemical properties of two leveling agents are compared
First, using cyclic voltammetric stripping, which was carried out in a
base solution with SPS and PEG, SPS, PEG, and MMT/AMT, respectively,
at two rotational speeds of 100 rpm and 1600 rpm, the effect of two
types of five-membered heterocyclic compounds with different side
chains on the electrodeposition behavior of copper was investigated.
The findings are depicted in Fig. 2. The observation of Fig. 2 reveals that
the dissolution peaks of copper obtained from electroplating solutions
containing two kinds of small molecule five membered heterocyclic
compounds additives are significantly smaller than those obtained from
the base plating solution whether at the 100 rpm or at the 1600 rpm. The
results of the aforementioned inquiry suggest that the introduction of
two small molecules consisting of five-membered heterocyclic com-
pounds can effectively enhance cathodic polarization and prevent the
deposition of copper. Moreover, it was further observed that the copper
dissolution peak was smaller when 5 ppm MMT was added than when 5
ppm AMT was added. This means that the additive MMT is superior to
AMT in inhibiting copper deposition through levelling agents.
The effects of the two levelling agents on copper electrodeposition
were explored further using linear scanning voltammetry (LSV), and the
findings are displayed in Fig. 3. From this, we can see when 5 ppm AMT
and 5 ppm MMT are added whether in weak or strong convection,
Copper’s deposition potential significantly shifts towards the negative
direction, which is consistent with the results obtained from CV, indi-
cating that the addition of AMT and MMT both can inhibit copper
electrodeposition. Moreover, Copper’s deposition potential attained in
the plating solution containing MMT shifts to the negative direction to
the greatest extent, indicating that the additive MMT has a greater
ability to suppress copper deposition compared to the additive AMT.

4. Conclusion
In summary, two small five-membered heterocyclic compounds with
different side chains, namely AMT and MMT, were selected as electro-
plated copper levelling agents in this paper. The electrochemical anal
ysis of CV, LSV, and GM showed that MMT has greater inhibitory ability
in inhibiting copper deposition behavior compared to AMT. An optima
concentration (7 ppm) of MMT added for effectively suppressing copper
deposition was obtained by electrochemical analysis from the CV, LSV,
and GM experiments based on the addition of different concentrations of
MMT additives. The blind hole filling experiment further demonstrates
that such an optimal addition concentration for MMT can achieve cop
per overfilling in high aspect ratio PCB blind holes. Characterization
analyses from FE-SEM, AFM, and XRD also further demonstrate that the
coating obtained at this optimal concentration of MMT has the densest
and smoothest surface with a typical 111 texture preferential growth.
The thermal shock experiment based on tin immersion indicates that the
copper layer obtained using MMT as a leveling agent has good reli
ability. It is indicated by in-situ Raman spectroscopy analysis that the
adsorption of MMT molecules on the electrode surface is a time
dependent process and the C–S, C–N, N––N, and - CH bonds are
preferentially adsorbed on the electrode surface. The smaller energy gap
value (ΔE = 3.729 (ev)) for the MMT molecule calculated by quantum
chemistry further indicates that suggest that the MMT molecules have
strong adsorption capacity. Furthermore, Quantum chemical calcula
tions based on the electronic potential energy of the MMT molecula
structure indicate that the thiol group, sulfur bond, and alkyl groups
from the MMT molecular belong to nucleophilic groups and provides the
preferred adsorption reaction active sites for interaction with the copper
surface, which is consistent with the results from the in situ electro-
chemical enhanced Raman spectroscopy. The adsorption of these
nucleophilic groups on the copper surface effectively inhibits copper
deposition and thereby achieving bottom-up copper overfilling in blind
holes. These results from the electrochemical analysis and theoretical
calculations fully demonstrate that MMT is an effective levelling agent
for PCB blind hole filling.
